source.title: The Knowledge Microscope: Features as Better Analytical Lenses than Neurons
source.authors: Yuheng Chen; Pengfei Cao; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly evaluates how well LLM-generated neuron explanations predict activations on new examples, and reports lower interpretability scores for neurons than for SAE features. This refines the claim that neurons are readily interpretable units.
record.gate_note: The relevant test is the adapted autointerpretation evaluation: an explainer receives high-activation examples and predicts activations on new examples. Feature/neuron ablation and privacy-erasure results concern other outcomes and do not directly test the listed claim versions. The paper does not report a percentage of neurons above a defined good-score threshold.
record.test_reason: The study adapts Bills et al.'s simulation scoring to factual triples in Gemma 2 2B/9B. gpt-4o-mini sees the top-3 activating examples and predicts activations on 6 new samples, and the correlation is scored. Neuron scores are low (mean IS 0.18 / 0.13; highly activated neurons below 0.4). This bears directly on V7 and on V6 in a new setting and domain.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE features beat neurons as units for factual knowledge: greater effect on knowledge expression, higher interpretability, stronger monosemanticity, and better privacy erasure via FeatureEdit.
record.recipe_differences: The study adapts LLM-based autointerpretation to factual triples: it selects 20 examples, provides the top 3 activations to gpt-4o-mini, and scores predictions on 6 new samples. It evaluates Gemma 2 2B and 9B rather than reproducing the original audit.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different IS values across model size and component type. Its evaluation uses one explainer, gpt-4o-mini, and six new samples per feature or neuron.

fits_no_version.finding: For relation-specific facts, neuron activations overlap across 0–100% relation-fact inputs and are already above zero with no relevant facts. Adjacent-ratio separation for neurons is weak at high ratios (Gemma 2B 80 vs 60: d = -0.13).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MLP neurons tied to factual relations also fire on unrelated facts, i.e. they are not single-job units in this domain.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The autointerpretation evaluation uses only 20 examples to form each explanation and 6 new examples for scoring. It tests only Gemma 2 2B and 9B with one explainer, and reports no proportion of neurons above a defined good-score threshold. The score values have no stated confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No additional relevant result rows left out. The paper's ablation, feature-distribution, and privacy-erasure outcomes do not measure the listed versions' claims about neuron explanation quality or the share of neurons with good automated scores.

untested.parts: No audit of neuron poles or shares with one or two jobs.
No shares of interpretable neurons across architectures or scale.
No vision models or analysis of canonical polysemantic neurons.
No manipulation of architecture, regularization or tools.
Only one explainer (gpt-4o-mini), so 'even with stronger explainers' is untested. No fraction of neurons above a good-score threshold is reported; only means and per-rank curves.
Explanations are not shown or inspected by humans. Only the prediction failure is measured, on factual triples only.

missing.what: Monosemanticity test: neuron activation distributions versus relation-fact proportion, with Cohen's d values for neurons. Bears loosely on 'one main job' (V1-like) but sits outside any version; worth a row for comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The neurons scored are a selected set (integrated-gradients knowledge neurons above a threshold), not a random sample, and scoring uses only 6 new samples per unit. Appendix C.2 describes the protocol for features, and its application to neurons is implied rather than detailed. The study reports means, not shares above a threshold, which limits direct comparison with V7's 'minority' framing. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of neuron poles or percentages of poles with one or multiple jobs.
The study uses Gemma 2 2B and 9B, but does not measure the claimed shares of interpretable neuron poles across models, architectures, or scale.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example, pose feature, or recursive-generalization analysis.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, or tool improvements as causes of changing neuron interpretability shares.
No attribution graphs or test of whether neuron-based graphs explain behavior without a replacement model.
The test is on factual-knowledge examples in Gemma 2 2B and 9B using gpt-4o-mini; it does not test other domains, models, or explainers.
The paper reports interpretability scores, not the fraction of neurons exceeding a defined good-score threshold. It tests one explainer, gpt-4o-mini, rather than comparing stronger explainer models.

rows.subject: Gemma 2 2B
rows.operation_detail: An LLM predicts neuron activations from selected high-activation examples; its predictions are correlated with actual activations on new examples.

conditions.value: threshold-selected units evaluated on the full dataset

rows.measure: Interpretability Score (IS), correlation between predicted and actual activations
rows.uncertainty: Paired comparison with post-MLP features: p < 0.001 (Table 4); no uncertainty interval for this score stated.
rows.note: Figure 7 gives the score; the paper describes post-MLP feature IS as about 4× the neuron score. The evaluation uses 20 samples to form an explanation, selects the top 3, and asks for predictions on 6 new samples.
rows.check: For V7 the low mean neuron IS (0.18) is the effect itself, so observed rather than partial. The neurons are integrated-gradients knowledge neurons selected by threshold, not a random sample.

relation.reason: Reports its own simulation-based interpretability scores for neurons, which bear on V6 and V7.

tranche.reason: New setting (integrated-gradients knowledge neurons on ParaRel factual triples in Gemma 2 2B/9B) with an adapted Bills et al. simulation score and a result on neuron scores. It argues for features over neurons but does not test the audit-share versions, so T5 is not needed.

source_check.notes: The Figure 7 means (0.18/0.13) come from threshold-selected knowledge neurons. The authors say averaging IS across the many neurons a fact activates biases the neuron score low, which is why they add per-unit Figure 6. Each IS is a correlation over only 6 samples (3 high, 3 random). The protocol is written for SAE features and applied to neurons.

statements.correction: 20 diverse samples are run through the model; the top 3 by activation go to gpt-4o-mini to form the explanation; it then predicts activations for 6 new samples (3 high-activation, 3 random); IS is the correlation (Appendix C.2).
statements.problem: Condition '20 examples per explanation' misstates the protocol: 20 samples are screened, and the explainer sees only the top 3.
